slides.title: Welcome to HTML Lists
slides.content:
# HTML Lists: Organizing Information 📋

Lists group related items into clean, readable structures. HTML provides three distinct types of lists for different semantic purposes.

## What you'll master:
- 🔘 **Unordered Lists (`<ul>`)** - Bulleted collections of related items
- 🔢 **Ordered Lists (`<ol>`)** - Sequenced, numbered procedures and rankings
- 📖 **Description Lists (`<dl>`)** - Key-value pairs, glossaries, and metadata
- 📂 **Nested Lists** - Multi-level hierarchies and tree structures
- 🎨 **Styling Lists** - Custom bullets, counters, and building navigation menus

slides.title: Ordered List Attributes
slides.content:
# Customizing Ordered Lists ⚙️ `
    ` supports three useful attributes for controlling numbering: ## 1. `type`: Numbering Style - `type="1"`: Decimal numbers (1, 2, 3...) - Default - `type="A"`: Uppercase letters (A, B, C...) - `type="a"`: Lowercase letters (a, b, c...) - `type="I"`: Uppercase Roman numerals (I, II, III...) - `type="i"`: Lowercase Roman numerals (i, ii, iii...) ## 2. `start`: Starting Index ```html_not
    1. Item fifty
    2. Item fifty-one
    ``` ## 3. `reversed`: Countdown ```html_not
    1. Lift off!
    2. Ignition
    3. Engine start
    ```

slides.title: Description Lists (<dl>)
slides.content:
# Description Lists (`<dl>`) 📖

Description lists (formerly called definition lists) represent name-value groups, glossaries, metadata, or FAQ lists.

## Three Component Tags:
1. `<dl>`: Description List container.
2. `<dt>`: **Description Term** — the term or label.
3. `<dd>`: **Description Details** — the explanation or value.

```html_not
<dl>
  <dt>HTML</dt>
  <dd>HyperText Markup Language - defines web structure.</dd>

  <dt>CSS</dt>
  <dd>Cascading Style Sheets - defines web presentation.</dd>

  <dt>JS</dt>
  <dd>JavaScript - adds interactive behavior.</dd>
</dl>
```

slides.title: Advanced Description Lists
slides.content:
# Multi-Term & Multi-Description Lists 📚

A description list can have multiple terms for a single description, or multiple descriptions for one term!

```html_not
<dl>
  <!-- Single term with multiple descriptions -->
  <dt>JavaScript</dt>
  <dd>A high-level, interpreted scripting language.</dd>
  <dd>Standardized under ECMAScript specifications.</dd>

  <!-- Multiple terms for the same meaning -->
  <dt>Color</dt>
  <dt>Colour</dt>
  <dd>Visual perceptual property derived from the spectrum of light.</dd>
</dl>
```

# Accessibility & Screen Readers ♿ Screen readers provide special announcement modes for HTML lists: - When encountering `
    ` or `
      `, the screen reader announces: *"List with 5 items"*. - For each item, it announces: *"Item 1 of 5"*, giving users clear structural awareness. > ⚠️ **CSS Reset Warning:** In Safari on iOS, applying `list-style: none` historically caused Safari to remove the list semantic role from the accessibility tree! To fix this in critical lists, add `role="list"`: ```html_not
      • Preserved semantic list item
      ```

slides.title: Best Practices for HTML Lists
slides.content:
# Best Practices Checklist ✅

1. ✅ **Use `<ol>` only when sequence matters:** If re-ordering items changes the meaning, use `<ol>`.
2. ✅ **Always nest directly in `<li>`:** Child lists must always reside inside parent `<li>` elements.
3. ✅ **Use `<dl>` for key-value pairs:** Stop using `<div>` pairs for product specifications, dictionaries, and definitions.
4. ✅ **Preserve list semantics in navigation:** Always build site navigation from `<nav><ul><li><a>`.

slides.title: Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# Lists Mastered! 🎉

You now know how to structure lists with semantic excellence and CSS finesse!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **Unordered (`<ul>`):** For non-sequential items with bullets.
- ✅ **Ordered (`<ol>`):** For sequential steps; customizable with `type`, `start`, and `reversed`.
- ✅ **Description (`<dl>`):** Pairs `<dt>` terms with `<dd>` definitions.
- ✅ **Nesting:** Always wrap sub-lists inside an `<li>`.
- ✅ **CSS Polish:** Style bullets with `::marker` and build navigation bars with `display: flex`.
